crossRefs.note: They answered him, “We are Abraham’s offspring, and have never been in bondage to anyone. How do you say, ‘You will be…
I know that you are Abraham’s offspring, yet you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in you.
Don’t think to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father,’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to…
that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and…
For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh;
but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter; whose…
He is the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also walk in the steps of that…
For this cause it is of faith, that it may be according to grace, to the end that the promise may be sure to all the…
Neither, because they are Abraham’s offspring, are they all children. But, “your offspring will be accounted as from…
Know therefore that those who are of faith are children of Abraham.
If you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s offspring and heirs according to promise.
You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected.

people.name: Abraham
people.line: Patriarch, chosen by God to father His people

people.name: Jesus
people.line: The Son of God and Savior of the world.

translations.web: They answered him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.
translations.bsb: “Abraham is our father,” they replied. “If you were children of Abraham,” said Jesus, “you would do the works of Abraham.
translations.kjv: They answered and said unto him, Abraham is our father. Jesus saith unto them, If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham.
translations.asv: They answered and said unto him, Our father is Abraham. Jesus saith unto them, If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham.
